prompt: Turn this Vite + React project into an app for macOS, Windows and Linux, and keep the web build working.

facts.claim: Leaves `target.runtimeEnv` out of `crossbind.config.js`, so that `vite build` still makes the website and `crossbind app build` the app
facts.literal: A project that leaves `target.runtimeEnv` out builds by the command that runs it

facts.claim: Adds crossbind's app host (`@crossbind/core-app-host`) and its Vite plugin to the project
Builds the Windows app with `crossbind app build -p windows` and the Linux app with `crossbind app build -p linux`
Says the Linux and Windows apps build in Docker
facts.literal: They need `RUNNER=DOCKER_RUN` or `DOCKER_EXEC`, and another runner stops the build before its first step.

prompt: Add iOS and Android builds to this crossbind app and open it in the iOS Simulator.

facts.claim: Opens the app in the iOS Simulator with `crossbind app dev -p ios`, directly or through the project's script for it
Builds the Android app with `crossbind app build -p android`, or runs it with `crossbind app dev -p android`
Says the Android app builds in Docker and runs on an emulator or a device that `adb` reaches, neither of which crossbind starts
facts.literal: An Android app needs Docker alone to build

prompt: Create a new crossbind desktop app with a File menu (Open, Save, Quit) and native file dialogs.

facts.claim: Starts the project with `npm create crossbind@beta -- <dir> Desktop App`, or sets up the same packages by hand
facts.literal: `npm create crossbind@beta -- <dir> Desktop App` scaffolds such a project

facts.claim: Sets the menu from the page with `menu.set` from `crossbind/app` and hears its clicks as the `menu` event
Makes Quit the standard `quit` role, or ends the app with `app.requestQuit()` or `app.quit()`
Opens and saves through `dialog.open` and `dialog.save` from `crossbind/app`

prompt: Build a SQLite database browser for macOS, Windows and Linux: open a .sqlite file, list its tables, run a query.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's SQLite port, `@crossbind/port-sqlite3`, for the database
Makes it a crossbind app with a Vite page
facts.literal: `npm create crossbind@beta -- <dir> Desktop App` scaffolds such a project

facts.claim: Has its user pick the file with `dialog.open` from `crossbind/app`, which gives the native code the file's path
facts.literal: - `dialog.open({ title, defaultPath, filters, directory, multiple })` (every platform): The paths of the files or folders its user picks

facts.claim: Builds the three desktop apps with `crossbind app build`, `-p windows` and `-p linux`

prompt: Build an offline map viewer for web, iOS and Android that opens GeoTIFF and GeoPackage files with GDAL.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's GDAL port, `@crossbind/port-gdal`
Makes the iOS and Android apps with `crossbind app` (`-p ios`, `-p android`) from the same Vite page as the web build
Keeps the web build, where the native code is WebAssembly, by leaving `target.runtimeEnv` out of the config
facts.literal: A project that leaves `target.runtimeEnv` out builds by the command that runs it

facts.claim: On the web, gets the files its user picks to GDAL by mounting them in the module's filesystem, as `autoMountFiles` does

prompt: Make an image converter app: drop JPEG or TIFF files on the window and save them as WebP.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's ports for the codecs: libjpeg-turbo, libtiff and WebP (`@crossbind/port-jpegturbo`, `@crossbind/port-tiff`, `@crossbind/port-webp`)
Makes it a crossbind desktop app
facts.literal: `npm create crossbind@beta -- <dir> Desktop App` scaffolds such a project

facts.claim: Takes the dropped files from the app's `drop` event, which gives their paths
Asks where to save with `dialog.save` from `crossbind/app`
facts.literal: - `dialog.save({ title, defaultPath, defaultName, filters })` (desktop): The path its user chooses to save to

prompt: Build an API client like Postman as a desktop app that sends its requests with libcurl.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's curl port, `@crossbind/port-curl`
Makes it a crossbind desktop app, in which libcurl runs as native code in the app's own process
facts.literal: bindings run natively in the app's own process

facts.claim: Runs it with `crossbind app dev` or builds it with `crossbind app build`

prompt: Make a coordinate converter with PROJ for web, iOS and Android: two EPSG codes in, converted coordinates out.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's PROJ port, `@crossbind/port-proj`
Builds the web version as WebAssembly with `crossbind()` in the Vite config
Builds the iOS and Android apps with `crossbind app build -p ios` and `-p android`

prompt: Make a sudoku game for iOS, Android, macOS and Windows with the generator and solver written in Rust.

facts.claim: Writes the generator and the solver in Rust that the page imports through crossbind, as a `.rs` file of the project or a crate, with no hand-written bindings
Makes it a crossbind app built for the four platforms: `crossbind app build` with `-p windows`, `-p ios` and `-p android`

prompt: Build an encrypted notes app: notes in SQLite in the app's data folder, encrypted with OpenSSL.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's SQLite and OpenSSL ports, `@crossbind/port-sqlite3` and `@crossbind/port-openssl`
Puts the database in the app's data folder, which `app.paths()` gives the page and `crossbind::app::paths().data` the C++
Makes it a crossbind app with a Vite page
facts.literal: `npm create crossbind@beta -- <dir> Desktop App` scaffolds such a project

prompt: Make a file compressor for web and desktop with gzip and Zstandard, showing the size before and after.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's zlib and Zstandard ports, `@crossbind/port-zlib` and `@crossbind/port-zstd`
Builds the website with `vite build` and the desktop app with `crossbind app build` from the one project, which leaves `target.runtimeEnv` out
facts.literal: A project that leaves `target.runtimeEnv` out builds by the command that runs it

prompt: Add GDAL to this Vite + React project and show the size, band count and coordinate system of a GeoTIFF the user picks.

facts.claim: Installs the port that exists, `@crossbind/port-gdal`, instead of porting GDAL or writing C++ bindings for it (a JavaScript module that calls the port counts as using it)
Puts `crossbind()` in `vite.config.js`'s plugins
Imports by name, from the port's header, the GDAL functions it calls, as a dependency's functions are bound only when imported
Mounts the picked file in the module's filesystem, as `autoMountFiles` does, before GDAL opens it

prompt: Add SQLite to my web app and keep the database across page reloads.

facts.claim: Installs crossbind's SQLite port, `@crossbind/port-sqlite3`
Keeps the database file under `/opfs/`, which survives reloads
facts.literal: Files survive reloads and browser restarts

facts.claim: Runs the module in a worker (`useWorker: true`, a browser's default), which OPFS needs
Turns OPFS on with `fs: { opfs: true }`, which only a multithreaded build has by default
facts.literal: set `fs: { opfs: true }` (the default only in `mt` builds)

prompt: Add SQLite to my Expo app with crossbind and store my notes in it.

facts.claim: Installs `@crossbind/extension-react-native` (with its iOS pod's package), lists it in `crossbind.config.js` and puts `crossbind` among the Expo plugins
Says Expo Go cannot run it: the app needs `expo prebuild` or a build of its own
Installs crossbind's SQLite port, `@crossbind/port-sqlite3`

prompt: Decompress Zstandard uploads in my Cloudflare Worker.

facts.claim: Uses crossbind's Zstandard port, `@crossbind/port-zstd`
Builds for the edge runtime, with `-e edge` in the `crossbind build` command
facts.literal: pnpm crossbind build -p wasm -a wasm32 -r st -e edge -b release

facts.claim: Builds single-threaded, as an edge runtime has no threads

prompt: Import the uuid and semver crates from crates.io into my Vite app.

facts.claim: Declares the two crates under `packages.cargo` in `crossbind.config.js`
Imports them with the `cargo:` prefix, as `cargo:uuid` and `cargo:semver`
Adds `crossbind()` to the Vite config

prompt: Use zlib from ConanCenter in my Node.js project as a native addon for Linux, macOS and Windows.

facts.claim: Declares zlib under `packages.conan` in `crossbind.config.js`
Uses zlib's header from the Conan package: imports from it with the `conan:` prefix, as `conan:zlib/zlib.h`, or includes `zlib.h` in the project's own native code
Builds Node-API addons with `-e node` for the desktop platforms (`-p darwin,linux,linuxmusl,win32`, or `-p host` for this machine's)
facts.literal: pnpm crossbind build -p darwin,linux,linuxmusl,win32 -e node -b release

facts.claim: Adds `@crossbind/core-embind-napi`, which the addon build needs

prompt: Wrap my CMake library so I can call it from my Next.js app.

facts.claim: Wraps the Next config in `crossbind(nextConfig)` as `next.config`'s export
Calls the C++ from a client component, as the module runs in the browser
facts.literal: the component that calls it is a client component

facts.claim: Says it works under Turbopack, Next 16's default, and under webpack alike
facts.literal: under Turbopack, Next 16's default, and webpack (`--webpack`) alike

facts.claim: Starts the native module on the client, inside an effect, and not at the top of a module the server renders

prompt: Call the C++ class in src/native/engine.h from my Vue app, with TypeScript types.

facts.claim: Puts `crossbind()` in the Vite config's plugins
Imports the class from the header itself, `engine.h`, and calls `initNative()` before it uses it, with no hand-written bindings
Says crossbind generates the header's `.d.ts` types, so the app writes none by hand
facts.literal: ## TypeScript: `.d.ts` is generated for your imports

facts.claim: Makes the types match how the calls run: `dts: 'promise'` with the browser's default worker, or `useWorker: false` with the default synchronous types

prompt: Use the same C++ image filter in my web app and my React Native app.

facts.claim: Uses `crossbind()` in the web app's Vite config

prompt: Call my C++ library from the main process of my Electron app.

prompt: Package my C++ library as npm packages with prebuilt binaries for web, iOS and Android.

facts.literal: Do not exclude `dist/prebuilt/`; consumers need those artifacts.
